nanananda_verbatim:
The ignorance in presuming that it is possible to go against the main
stream of the three signata — impermanence, suffering and not-self — is
the place of its origin. That heap of preparations impelled by ignorance,
which takes the current forward, may be regarded as sankharas. And where
the current in its progress clashes with the main stream to become a
whirlpool, that pushing forward against the main stream is vinnana or
consciousness. The outcome of the clash is nama-rupa, or name-and-form,
with its formal name and nominal form.
plain_english_below: The not seeing how it works in presuming that it is possible to go against the main stream of the three signata — impermanence, suffering and not-self — is the place of its origin. That heap of things the mind makes impelled by not seeing how it works, which takes the current forward, may be regarded as sankhara (things the mind makes)s. And where the current in its progress clashes with the main stream to become a whirlpool, that pushing forward against the main stream is vinnana (just knowing, before words) or consciousness. The outcome of the clash is nama-rupa (names laid on top of what you see and hear), or name-and-form, with its formal name and nominal form.
tts_line: The not seeing how it works in presuming that it is possible to go against the main stream of the three signata — impermanence, suffering and not-self — is the place of its origin. That heap of things the mind makes impelled by not seeing how it works, which takes the current forward, may be regarded as sankhara — things the mind makes — s. And where the current in its progress clashes with the main stream to become a whirlpool, that pushing forward against the main stream is vinnana — just knowing, before words — or consciousness. The outcome of the clash is nama-rupa — names laid on top of what you see and hear —, or name-and-form, with its formal name and nominal form.

nanananda_verbatim:
Just as a woman or a man, youthful and fond of adornment, in looking
at her or his facial image in a mirror or in a bowl filled with pure,
clear, clean water, would be seeing it with dependence and not without
dependence.
plain_english_below: Just as a woman or a man, youthful and fond of adornment, in looking at her or his facial image in a mirror or in a bowl filled with pure, clear, clean water, would be seeing it with dependence and not without dependence.

nanananda_verbatim:
The prefix upa in upadana conveys the sense of proximity or nearness...
So the totality of existence, from the point of view of Dhamma, is
dependent on a holding on, or a grasping on.
plain_english_below: The prefix upa in upadana (holding on) conveys the sense of proximity or nearness... So the totality of existence, from the point of view of Dhamma, is dependent on a holding on, or a holding on on.
tts_line: The prefix upa in upadana — holding on — conveys the sense of proximity or nearness... So the totality of existence, from the point of view of Dhamma, is dependent on a holding on, or a holding on on.

nanananda_verbatim:
It is with dependence, friend Ananda, that the notion 'am' occurs, not
without dependence. With dependence on form... on feeling... on
perception... on preparations... on consciousness does the notion 'am'
occur.
plain_english_below: It is with dependence, friend Ananda, that the notion 'am' occurs, not without dependence. With dependence on form... on pleasant-or-unpleasant tone... on perception... on things the mind makes... on consciousness does the notion 'am' occur.
tts_line: It is with dependence, friend Ananda, that the notion 'am' occurs, not without dependence. With dependence on form... on pleasant-or-unpleasant tone... on perception... on things the mind makes... on consciousness does the notion 'am' occur.

nanananda_verbatim:
The cessation of the puny centre of the whirlpool is equivalent to
inheriting an expansive great ocean. To give up the limitations of a
vortex, is to inherit the limitless ocean.
plain_english_below: The stopping of the puny centre of the whirlpool is equivalent to inheriting an expansive great ocean. To give up the limitations of a vortex, is to inherit the limitless ocean.
tts_line: The stopping of the puny centre of the whirlpool is equivalent to inheriting an expansive great ocean. To give up the limitations of a vortex, is to inherit the limitless ocean.

nanananda_verbatim:
In this way, he directed his radical reflection gradually upwards...
and at last came to the saṃsāric vortex between consciousness and
name-and-form.
plain_english_below: In this way, he directed his radical reflection gradually upwards... and at last came to the samsaric vortex between consciousness and name-and-form.
tts_line: In this way, he directed his radical reflection gradually upwards... and at last came to the samsaric vortex between consciousness and name-and-form.

nanananda_verbatim:
When consciousness leaves this body and comes to stay in a mother's
womb, when it is fully established there, 'that' place becomes a 'this'
place. From the point of view of that consciousness, the 'there' becomes
a 'here'. Consequently, from the new point of view, what was earlier a
'here', becomes a 'there'.
plain_english_below: When consciousness leaves this body and comes to stay in a mother's womb, when it is fully established there, 'that' place becomes a 'this' place. From the point of view of that consciousness, the 'there' becomes a 'here'. Consequently, from the new point of view, what was earlier a 'here', becomes a 'there'.
tts_line: When consciousness leaves this body and comes to stay in a mother's womb, when it is fully established there, 'that' place becomes a 'this' place. nanananda_verbatim:
Kimhi nu kho sati jarāmaraṇaṃ hoti, kiṃ paccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ?
Jātiyā kho sati jarāmaraṇaṃ hoti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ — 'What
being there, does decay and death come to be? Conditioned by what, is
decay-and-death? Birth being there does decay-and-death come to be,
conditioned by birth.'
plain_english_below: Kimhi nu kho sati (remembering to notice) jaramaranam hoti, kim paccaya jaramaranam? Jatiya kho remembering to notice jaramaranam hoti, jatipaccaya jaramaranam — 'What being there, does decay and death come to be? Conditioned by what, is decay-and-death? Birth being there does decay-and-death come to be, conditioned by birth.'
tts_line: Kimhi nu kho sati — remembering to notice — jaramaranam hoti, kim paccaya jaramaranam? Jatiya kho remembering to notice jaramaranam hoti, jatipaccaya jaramaranam — 'What being there, does decay and death come to be? Conditioned by what, is decay-and-death? Birth being there does decay-and-death come to be, conditioned by birth.'

sorrows, grieves, and laments;

nanananda_verbatim:
That way, what actually is involved here, is a change of point of view.
So it does not mean completely leaving one place and going to another,
as is usually meant by the journey of an individual. The process, then,
is a sort of going round and round.
plain_english_below: That way, what actually is involved here, is a change of point of view. So it does not mean completely leaving one place and going to another, as is usually meant by the journey of an individual. The process, then, is a sort of going round and round.

nanananda_verbatim:
This-ness and otherwise-ness imply a circuit. It is a circuit between
a 'here' and a 'there'. It is a turning round, an alternation or a
circuitous journey. It is like a rotation on the spot. It is an
ambivalence between a here and a there.
plain_english_below: This-ness and otherwise-ness imply a circuit. It is a circuit between a 'here' and a 'there'. It is a turning round, an alternation or a circuitous journey. It is like a rotation on the spot. It is an ambivalence between a here and a there.
